response.justification: The candidate is a highly experienced, versatile senior engineer with 15+ years across web, backend, mobile and some embedded work, plus strong evidence of ownership, mentoring, testing discipline and technical communication. However, the role is fundamentally a C++ engineering position in industrial automation, and the candidate's C++ exposure is limited to roughly seven months at National Instruments in 2014–2015 and a university thesis project — over a decade ago. There is no evidence of STL-heavy modern C++, MQTT/Modbus/OPC UA protocols, IEC 62443 / SDL secure engineering, Azure, or industrial automation domain experience. The transferable skills (low-latency services in D, event-driven architecture, multi-threading/async I/O, message-driven microservices) are real but would require a substantial ramp on the core technology and regulated-security aspects of the job.
strengths: Deep experience with low-latency, event-driven, high-throughput distributed systems
Strong engineering craftsmanship: TDD, CI/CD, tooling, mentoring, workshops and public talks
Broad polyglot background including some C/C++ and embedded/hardware-adjacent work
concerns: C++ experience is minimal and over ten years stale; not a listed current skill
No industrial automation, IoT protocol (MQTT/Modbus/OPC UA) or IEC 62443/SDL security experience
Recent career trajectory is web/TypeScript full-stack, diverging from the systems C++ focus

key_factors.factor: Missing industrial cybersecurity (IEC 62443/SDL) and automation domain
Senior-level distributed/concurrent systems and mentoring track record
